speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. To better understand your condition, could you please describe where exactly you are experiencing double vision and whether the weakness in your upper limbs is on one side or both? REQUEST TEST: Blood test for thyroid function and acetylcholine receptor antibodies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood test for thyroid function: NORMAL READINGS; Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. To further narrow down the cause of your symmetrical weakness and diplopia, have you noticed any muscle twitching or drooping eyelids recently? REQUEST TEST: Electromyography (EMG) and REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electromyography: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation; MRI Brain: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The EMG findings of decreased response with repetitive stimulation combined with your symmetrical weakness and diplopia strongly suggest a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you experienced any ptosis (drooping of the eyelids) or difficulty swallowing? DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
